key_insight: Input-convex neural surrogates let lane-changing planners model safety and comfort through linear programming embeddings without binary variables.
engineering_relevance: The framework makes learned traffic-interaction models more tractable for connected and automated vehicle trajectory planning in mixed traffic.
method: Plan lane-changing trajectories using Bézier curves.
Predict safety costs with recurrent, fully input-convex, and partially input-convex networks; approximate lateral comfort costs with a separate input-convex network.
Embed surrogates using LP formulations with theoretically established exactness at optimality.
evidence_signal: Tests on hybrid real-world and simulated trajectories report competitive surrogate accuracy and faster optimization than conventional MIPs; closed-loop simulations report lower weighted planning costs than baselines.
watch_item: Exactness of the optimization embedding does not guarantee real-world safety when learned surrogates encounter unfamiliar traffic behavior.
paper_title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks
